problem:
Let $V=C[0,2\pi ]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,2\pi ],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨f(t),g(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }f(t)g(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Given the functions $f(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$ and $g(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),$ which of the following statements are true?

- $⟨f(t),g(t)⟩=\pi $
- $⟨f(t),g(t)⟩=2\pi $
- $f(t)⊥g(t)$ with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V$

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the identity $\operatorname{sin}⁡\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡\beta =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\alpha -\beta )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\alpha +\beta )).$*
